newsitem.title: USA: Texas elephant's death blamed on infection, abuse.
newsitem.headline: Texas elephant's death blamed on infection, abuse.

text.p: A circus elephant found dead here last week was killed by a salmonella infection and mistreatment, a zoo official said Monday.

A second elephant from the same Texas-based circus was also thought to be infected by the bacteria, but was responding well to antibiotics, said Kent Newton, assistant director of the Albuquerque Biological Park.
Newton said both animals were severely undernourished and weighed at least a thousand pounds less than their minimum ideal weight of 3,500 pounds.
Albuquerque police discovered the dead elephant Thursday in an unventilated trailer parked in the sun. They estimated the temperature inside the vehicle to be 120 degrees.
Two other elephants, including the one now on antibiotics, and eight llamas were also in the trailer. The heat and poor conditions contributed to the elephant's death, Newton said.
Newton said the salmonella infection could have been contracted by eating spoiled food or from other animals.

The city obtained a temporary restraining order to care for the animals at least until a hearing Wednesday. The third elephant and all the llamas appeared to be in good condition, but were under observation, Newton said.

The animals belong to the King Royal Circus of San Antonio, Texas, and were being transported back to Texas from an appearance in Nevada when the elephant died. Animal handler Ben Davenport, 23, of Laredo, Texas, has been cited on suspicion of cruelty to animals, a charge he denied.

A U.S. Department of Agriculture spokesman said the circus was fined $8,000 last year for animal care violations. Davenport said the trailer carrying the animals had been inspected and approved by the USDA 10 days ago in Nevada.
